article_title: Worried about taking a sick day? What that says about you

tasks.prompt: What is the article mainly examining?
options: Why people work while ill and how personal traits and workplace culture influence that choice
Why younger workers suffer more long-term illness than older workers
How employers can eliminate every absence from work
Why remote work has made sick leave unnecessary
tasks.correct_answer: Why people work while ill and how personal traits and workplace culture influence that choice
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה בוחנת presenteeism — עבודה בזמן מחלה — ואת השפעת הזהות האישית, הפחד, תנאי העבודה ותרבות הארגון.

tasks.prompt: What do the cited UK figures show about sick leave among different age groups?
options: Both groups took an average of 6.2 days
Workers aged 16–24 took 2.4 days, compared with 6.2 for those aged 50–64
Workers aged 50–64 took only 2.4 days
Age made no measurable difference
tasks.correct_answer: Workers aged 16–24 took 2.4 days, compared with 6.2 for those aged 50–64
tasks.explanation_hebrew: נתוני ONS מצביעים על 2.4 ימי מחלה בגילי 16–24 לעומת 6.2 ימים בגילי 50–64.

tasks.prompt: What does “presenteeism” mean in the article?
options: Taking planned annual leave
Working only from an office
Continuing to work even when sick
Being absent without informing a manager
tasks.correct_answer: Continuing to work even when sick
tasks.explanation_hebrew: presenteeism הוא מצב שבו אדם ממשיך להגיע לעבודה או לעבוד מרחוק אף שהוא חולה.

options: A job located in a city centre
A rule requiring staff to attend headquarters
A system for sharing tasks among colleagues
The degree to which work is central to a person's identity
tasks.correct_answer: The degree to which work is central to a person's identity
tasks.explanation_hebrew: work centrality מתארת עד כמה העבודה היא חלק מרכזי בזהותו של האדם, ולכן היעדרות יכולה להרגיש כאובדן חלק מעצמו.

tasks.prompt: Why can understaffed teams make employees reluctant to take legitimate sick leave?
options: They know their absence will add work for colleagues
They receive extra holiday whenever a colleague is absent
They are legally required to work through illness
They can no longer contact their managers
tasks.correct_answer: They know their absence will add work for colleagues
tasks.explanation_hebrew: כאשר אין גיבוי והצוות מתוח, העובד עלול לחוש אשמה משום שהיעדרותו תגדיל את העומס על עמיתיו.

tasks.prompt: According to Dr Audrey Tang, how long should someone stay home after a fever has passed?
options: 48 hours
24 hours
One working week
Only until the next morning
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ההמלצה המצוטטת היא להישאר בבית 24 שעות לאחר שחלף חום; לאחר הקאות ושלשול מדובר ב־48 שעות.

tasks.prompt: Give the article's main explanations for why younger workers may record fewer sick days.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לציין חוסר ביטחון תעסוקתי, מצב בריאותי, רצון ליצור רושם וציפיות בנוגע לרווחה נפשית.
expected_points: Younger workers may have insecure jobs such as zero-hours contracts
They are less likely to have long-term health conditions
They are less likely to have joint problems
People early in their careers may fear appearing weak or lazy
They may worry about making a negative impression
They may also have higher expectations that employers respect mental wellbeing

tasks.prompt: Explain how managers can unintentionally create a culture that rewards working while ill.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר מסרים עקיפים כגון שבח על עבודה בזמן מחלה, חשדנות כלפי היעדרות, עדיפות לתפוקה והיעדר גיבוי.
expected_points: Managers may praise employees who work through illness
Routine questioning of sick leave signals distrust
Prioritising productivity over health creates guilt and shame
Lack of cover makes employees feel responsible for colleagues' workload
Workers absorb the message that attendance matters more than recovery
Open and honest conversations can counter this culture

tasks.prompt: Summarise how individual identity, job insecurity and workplace culture affect decisions about sick leave.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לסכם באנגלית את work centrality, הפחד משיפוט, תנאי העבודה, תרבות ארגונית והיחס לבריאות נפשית ופיזית.
expected_points: A third to a half of people may work while sick
Strong work centrality can make absence feel like losing part of oneself
Caring professionals may feel a duty to keep showing up
Young or insecure workers may fear a negative impression
Understaffing and toxic productivity cultures create guilt
Healthy workplaces encourage honest discussion and trust
Mental and physical inability to work should be treated equally

tasks.prompt: Write practical guidance for employees deciding whether they are well enough to work.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב הנחיות מאוזנות באנגלית הכוללות תסמינים, יכולת לתפקד, עבודה מהבית, בריאות נפשית וטיפול עצמי.
expected_points: Assess capacity to perform the job safely and effectively
Stay home for 48 hours after vomiting or diarrhoea stops
Stay home for 24 hours after a fever passes
Consider working from home for mild coughs or colds when appropriate
Treat mental health like physical health
Check sleep, self-care and ability to decompress
Communicate honestly with the employer
Do not let guilt replace a health-based decision
